common_name: Charlie's Michelle Louisiana Iris (Ruffled Pink Louisiana Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in fall for best root establishment ahead of spring bloom; keep the bed consistently moist to wet through the growing season, as Louisiana iris rhizomes dry out and decline quickly if allowed to bake in dry soil.

directions: Plant rhizomes shallowly in consistently moist to wet, fertile, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light partial shade. Charlie's Michelle is a Louisiana iris cultivar prized for its ruffled, orchid-pink flowers with a warm glow at the throat, blooming amid the peak Louisiana iris season in mid-spring. Like other Louisiana iris hybrids it descends from Gulf Coast wetland species and performs best where soil never fully dries out, making it well suited to a pond margin, ditch bank, or heavily irrigated border bed. Topdress with compost each fall, keep water levels up through spring bloom, and divide crowded clumps every four to five years after flowering to keep vigor and bloom count high.
sources: Louisiana State University AgCenter — Louisiana Iris Culture and Varieties

planting.note: Plant divisions in consistently moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to light partial shade; Japanese iris need steady moisture through the growing season and are best sited at a pond margin or in a heavily irrigated bog-style bed.

directions: Plant divisions in consistently moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to light partial shade. Rose Queen is an older, classic Japanese iris cultivar bearing single, flat-form flowers in a soft rosy-pink to rose-lavender shade, a warmer color note than the blues and violets that dominate most Japanese iris breeding. It shares the species' demand for steady moisture and acidic soil, declining quickly in dry or alkaline conditions, so it is best grown at a pond edge or in a bed that can be kept damp all summer. Mulch to conserve soil moisture, avoid lime-based amendments, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in early fall to renew vigor and bloom.

directions: Plant divisions in consistently moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to light partial shade. Frilled Enchantment is a Japanese iris cultivar selected for its heavily ruffled, crepe-textured petals, giving the large flat blooms an especially lacy, ornate appearance compared with plainer-edged Japanese iris forms. As with all Japanese iris, it needs steady moisture and acidic soil through the growing season and sulks quickly if the bed dries out or is amended with lime, so a pond margin or consistently irrigated bed suits it best. Site out of the strongest wind to protect the delicate, frilled petal edges, mulch to hold moisture, and divide every three to four years in early fall to keep clumps vigorous.
